pied.devise: “To know Christ and to make Him known”
pied.appartenance: University Bible Group of Morocco — a member of IFES, Middle East and North Africa region.

commun.themeTexte: The fourth year of the ten-year vision, on Acts 2:42. Fellowship is first something received: because God calls us into fellowship with His Son, we can be in fellowship with one another — never mere affinity, but the fruit of one same life received.
commun.envoiReussiTexte: The National Secretariat has received it. Someone will reply and put you in touch with the group nearest your campus — and if no one answers within a week, write again: your message got lost.
commun.envoiRefuseChamps: Something is missing. Check your name, how to reach you, and your message.
commun.envoiRefuseIndisponible: The message did not go through: the site cannot reach its database. We would rather tell you than leave you waiting for a reply that would never come. Please try again later.

accueil.display: To know Christ and to make Him known.
accueil.accroche: The GBU is a family. It meets on campus every week — and in homes too, around a meal, a prayer, a passage of the Bible. People often arrive alone, far from home; they find brothers and sisters.
accueil.pratique1Texte: Every week, in a small group, following the year's study outline.
accueil.pratique2Texte: For one another, for the campuses, for the country.
accueil.pratique3Texte: Arriving alone in a country you don't know is hard. The group is often the first family.
accueil.pratique4Texte: Camps, conventions and national gatherings bring together students from every city. And in between: shared meals, outings, sport, fellowship.
accueil.galerieTitre: The movement, as it is lived.
accueil.rejoindreTitre: There may be a group right next to you.
accueil.rejoindreTexte: Tell us which city you study in: someone from the movement will reply, and put you in touch with the students closest to your campus.

leMouvement.eyebrow: A member of IFES · MENA region
leMouvement.accroche: The GBUM brings together students who want to live out and deepen their Christian faith during their years of study, in Morocco's university cities. A member is called a GBUssien.
leMouvement.devise: “To know Christ and to make Him known”
leMouvement.visionNom: Scouts of the campuses for Christ
leMouvement.visionTexte: Born while preparing the 2023 Ifrane camp, this vision carries the movement for ten years.
leMouvement.visionAnnee: Year 4 of 10. Each year one segment of the vision is worked through in the Bible study outline — this year, the fellowship of disciples.
leMouvement.histoireTexte: Where the movement comes from, and how it got here.
leMouvement.frise1947: IFES is founded at Harvard University by representatives of ten national movements. Headquarters in Oxford.
leMouvement.frise1968: The GBUAF — French-speaking Africa's University Bible Groups — is born at a gathering of some fifteen students in Abidjan. Most GBUssiens in Morocco come from that region.
leMouvement.frise2023: Ifrane Camp: the movement gives itself a ten-year vision, running to 2033.
leMouvement.organisationTitre: Five levels, from national to cell group.
leMouvement.niveau1Texte: The National Secretary and their assistants, who oversee the movement in Morocco.
leMouvement.niveau2Texte: Renewed every year. Each member carries a national responsibility; some accompany a city.
leMouvement.niveau3Texte: One committee per city, renewed every year.
leMouvement.niveau4Texte: In neighbourhoods or on campus. This is where the Bible studies take place. Their leaders are renewed every year.
leMouvement.niveau5Texte: Former GBUssiens who support the movement — financially, in prayer, and in other ways.
leMouvement.renvoiTexte: The university cities where the GBUM is present.
leMouvement.familleTexte: The GBU is a family. It meets on campus every week — and in homes too, around a meal, a prayer, a passage of the Bible. People often arrive alone, far from home; they find brothers and sisters.

ouNousSommes.accroche: The university cities of Morocco where GBUM students meet. Tell us yours: someone will put you in touch with those closest to your campus.
ouNousSommes.aucuneVilleTexte: Write to us anyway. There is almost always a neighbouring city, there is the Ifrane camp where students from all over Morocco gather, and there is the possibility of starting a group where you study.

leCanevas.accroche: Each year the movement publishes an outline: the sequence of Bible studies that every group in the movement follows. Past outlines remain open to all.
leCanevas.archivesTexte: The movement's study material, open to all. Coming soon.
leCanevas.ensembleTitre: The outline is meant to be lived together.
leCanevas.ensembleTexte: It is written to be opened together, out loud, with people. Tell us where you study: we will put you in touch with the nearest group.
leCanevas.couverture: Cover of the 2026-2027 study material: silhouettes holding hands before a cross at sunset, beneath the title “The brotherly fellowship of disciples”

nousEcrire.eyebrow: A question, a request, a proposal
nousEcrire.accroche: Your message comes straight to us. Someone will reply, and put you in touch with the group closest to your campus.
nousEcrire.nomIndice: First name, or first and last name
nousEcrire.messageIndice: Tell us in a few words what brings you here.
nousEcrire.devenirTitre: It comes to us, and to us alone.
nousEcrire.devenirTexte: It appears nowhere publicly. You can ask for it to be erased at any time.
nousEcrire.chercheGroupeTexte: The “Join” path is quicker: a single form, no account, and the National Secretariat points you to the nearest group.

rejoindre.accroche: Tell us which city you study in and how to reach you. Someone from the movement will reply, and put you in touch with the students closest to your campus.
rejoindre.motIndice: I've just arrived and I don't know anyone.
rejoindre.viePriveeTexte: It goes to the National Secretariat, and to it alone. You can ask for it to be deleted at any time.
rejoindre.autreCasEyebrow: Another case — no group in your city
rejoindre.autreCasTitre: No group where you are, yet.
rejoindre.autreCasTexte: But you are not at the end of the road. This case is treated with the same care as any other: it is where someone is lost, or caught.
rejoindre.option1Texte: Students there welcome those who come from elsewhere.
rejoindre.option2Texte: Every student in Morocco meets there. You can come.
rejoindre.option3Texte: Every group began with one student who wrote in.
rejoindre.informeTexte: The day a group opens in your city, you will hear about it. That is the only thing we will use your address for.
rejoindre.formulaireTexte: Someone will reply. Nobody else sees this message.
